podcast.body: Recorded in 1965 and featured on "The Fugs First Album," "CIA Man" is recognized as the first instance of anyone deliberately dropping an F-bomb on a rock and roll record. The use of such language was groundbreaking and controversial for its time, still necessitating censorship for broadcast decades later. "And that, as far as we know, is the first time anyone anywhere in the world dropped the F-bomb on a rock and roll record. Deliveredly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Ongoing History Book of Firsts

podcast.body: Recorded in 1965, this song by The Fugs is documented as the first record to deliberately feature obvious "F-bombs," marking a significant moment in the history of explicit language in recorded music. "And in 1965, they recorded a song called C.I.A. Man. And it featured plenty of obvious F-bombs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
